newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea arrests U.S. businessman for spying.
newsitem.headline: South Korea arrests U.S. businessman for spying.

text.p: South Korea's top intelligence agency said it had arrested an American businessman on Wednesday for spying.

A spokesman for the Agency for National Security Planning said Donald Ratcliffe, 62, whom it identified as a director in charge of Asian operations at U.S.-based Litton Guidance and Controls Systems, was suspected of collecting military secrets in South Korea.
"The American was arrested today for collecting military secrets here," the official told Reuters.
A U.S. embassy spokesman said he had no information on the case. The U.S. military spokesman in South Korea, where the United States has 36,450 troops, was not immediately available for comment.
No one was available for comment at Litton Industries in California.

Earlier on Wednesday the U.S. military denied a report by South Korea's Chosun Ilbo newspaper that Ratcliffe had been hiding at a major U.S. military camp in Seoul. The report also said U.S. military officials refused to hand him over to South Korean authorities.
"That part of the article is an absolute lie. We have been coordinating very closely with the Seoul Prosecutor's Office," the U.S. military said in a statement.
"There has been no request to the USFK (U.S. Forces Korea) for assistance. We will, as always, cooperate with the ROK (Republic of Korea) authorities," it said.
Last September U.S. prosecutors arrested a Korean-born U.S. citizen on charges of passing more than 40 classified documents to a South Korean embassy official since May.

One week later a U.S. district judge overturned an earlier ruling by a magistrate that Robert Kim, a U.S. Navy computer specialist, be kept in jail pending his trial. The judge ordered that Kim be kept in jail pending his trial for espionage.
